question: Ticket 1515f3b2ee29 says 'build commit lands its seal when rung 4 admits ticket via CAIRN_RESEAL_RULING ruling', but outline 9.4.2.3.3 reads "Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged." (outline requires seal to hold while code unchanged (representing proof validation); if ruling determines seal-recording independent of proof status, the seal no longer embodies validation but judgment instead). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; there is no conflict. A ruling never sets a verdict: reseal asks rung4_refusal before anything runs, and an admitted id only lets the proof run over bytes that moved under an open ladder. The seal then records what that run measured, green or red. The ticket changes only who carries the id, the hook instead of a hand typing --ruling, so a seal still holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
